did_you_know.text: Did you know? Micah portrays the mountains and hills as being summoned to hear the LORD’s case against His people, presenting creation as a witness to the rebuke.
Did you know? The LORD reminds Israel of the Exodus from Egypt and of His sending Moses, along with Aaron and Miriam, as examples of His faithfulness and leadership of the people.
Did you know? The LORD recalls Balak’s plan and Balaam’s answer, as well as the journey from Shittim to Gilgal, so that Israel may recognize the LORD’s righteous acts.
Did you know? Micah presents the LORD’s central requirement: to do justice, love mercy, and walk humbly with God.
Did you know? The chapter describes treasures gained through wickedness and a short measure, meaning a dishonest commercial measure.
Did you know? The use of dishonest scales and deceptive weights is presented in the chapter as conduct that prevents a person from being considered innocent and upright.
Did you know? The punishment described includes eating without being satisfied, being unable to escape, and losing one’s produce; it is presented as the result of sin.
Did you know? Micah links the people’s condition to following the statutes of Omri and the practices of the house of Ahab, warning of desolation, disgrace, and astonishment.
